stops.name: Ardastra Gardens, Zoo and Conservation Centre
stops.en: Visit the Bahamas' only zoo. See the marching flamingo shows. Let the parakeets land on you as you feed them.

stops.name: National Art Gallery of The Bahamas
stops.en: Opened in 2003, this showcases Bahamian art from the precolonial era to the present. The quality of art is rather uneven to say the least, but the renovated building — once the residence of the Chief Justice — is a sight in itself.

stops.name: Fort Fincastle
stops.en: A small fort built in 1793 which overlooks the city of Nassau from a small hill south of town. Several cannons are on display. Tours are conducted daily 8AM-3PM.

stops.name: Pirates of Nassau
stops.en: Recreations of a pirate town, a pirate ship and a pirate battle, with a few real artifacts mixed in. Cheesy, but fun. Try to catch a guided tour.

eats.name: The Shoal Restaurant and Lounge
eats.note: If the tourist crowds are getting you down, take a taxi out to where the locals eat. Enjoy fish that falls off the bone, friendly service, and a dessert of guava

eats.name: Cafe Matisse
eats.note: Tucked away on a quiet lane, Matisse serves excellent Italian food with fresh local ingredients. Reservations recommended; try to get a seat in the delightful garden courtyard, which is shady by day a

eats.name: Señor Frogs
eats.note: Next to the cruise dock, beside a stinky sewer pipe. Check which way the wind is blowing before you order. Doesn't serve Kalik.

eats.name: Club Waterloo
eats.note: On the north side of the island, about two miles from the dock.

eats.name: Cocktails and Dreams
eats.note: Draws a sketchier crowd, although it is on the beach. Come here in a group.

eats.name: Club Fluid
eats.note: Draws a very local crowd. You will get lots of recommendations from Bahamians you meet, but it is not a tourist club at all.

next.name: Paradise Island
next.note: Paradise Island, just across a bridge from Nassau. It is home to the lavish Atlantis hotel and resort.
